answer: One Sybil defense is proof-of-unique-work tied to hardware cost: each new identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle whose difficulty rises like a tide with the number of recent signups. A cipher-bound nonce makes the proof single-use, so it can't be replayed across accounts. An attacker spinning up many fake agents pays memory and time per identity, and each extra one raises the difficulty for the whole batch, so a plume of cheap clones becomes uneconomic.
